note: Inputs of tools/perf/frame_budget.py (docs/PERF.md section 11). Every number is an estimate [E] until a measurement replaces it: frameprof per-thread counts (--frameprof) for the CPU work, the render machine's report (--render) for the renderer. Instruction counts are per frame, in millions (M), for one exterior Mojave frame with the native renderer (S6n), as [lo, hi]. basis: E estimate, M measured. Each item names its subsystem; hotspot_functions are the per-function proxies (A64 instructions per call from dyncount [M] x calls per frame [E]) and fixes the optimization queue per subsystem (frame_budget.py hotspots[], docs/PERF.md 11.4).
scene: exterior, Mojave wasteland, ~2,500 draws (RENDER_NATIVE draw counts), native renderer

assumptions.note: A57 on pointer-chasing engine code; SPEC CPU2006 int on A57-class cores ~1.0-1.2, games lower. Replaced by benchmark B1 (PERF.md 9) on hardware.
Switch CPU: 1020 MHz stock (docked and handheld); 1785 MHz boost (the owner's console can run it, J-0132).
cores 0-2 for the application; core 3 is the system's, usable with the core3=1 opt-in (S5 33c0b1b).
work moved off the main thread runs this much as fast on a worker core (cold caches, hand-off waits, migration inside the 0b110 mask).
per-frame hand-offs: ~20 events, the AI spin lock 0x011f11a0, stage semaphores (PERF.md 6.1); B3 measures it.
worst frame / mean frame for 'stable' targets (cell streaming, AI bursts, Havok contacts). 45 fps stable means the worst frame fits 22.2 ms.

60 fps stable: worst frame 16.7 ms at the 1.02 GHz stock clock (the owner's target, J-0150)
